subject: Do I need add a intercept to the basic BYM model?

messages.author: ff1a5632abbf2fe9
messages.subject: Do I need add a intercept to the basic BYM model?
parts:
Hi, just emailed this questions to the he...@r-inla.org, but I think this is a publicly interesting questions

I read two papers from INLA team. Both of them has R code in the paper.
A:  A primer on disease mapping and ecological regression using INLA. B Schrödle, L Held - Computational statistics, 2011 - Springer
B:  Spatial and Spatio-Temporal models with R-INLA. M Blangiardo, M Cameletti, G Baio, H Rue - Spatial and Spatio-temporal Epidemiology, 2013 - Elsevier

In paper A, authors explicitly point out that "For the besag prior a sum-to-zero" constraint is imposed as default'. However, there is no intercept term in the R code. Like this,
formula<-Y~f(region.struct,model="bym",graph.file="germany.graph")

In contrast, authors of paper B includes the a intercept term, which is specified by adding  term  "1"  in the R code. Like this, 
formula<-Y~1 + f(region.struct,model="bym",graph.file="germany.graph")

PS: in WinBugs geobugs12 manual, the author explicitly says adding a intercept term is essential in the BYM model, as the random effect terms include a sum-to-zero constraint.


If the strategy in paper B is correct, there is another question.
In winbugs, the intercept term is regarded as a parameter, which must be assigned an improper uniform prior. How can we accomplish this by adding a term "1"? Is this default in INLA?


Thank you in advance
Xing

messages.author: bbb9357156c132fe
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Do I need add a intercept to the basic BYM model?
parts:
Hi,
The formula environment in R automatically adds an intercept, so both formulas are the same. 

In INLA, the intercept is (rightly!) considered part of the Gaussian term and has a diffuse Gaussian prior on it. You can control the precision (inverse variance) of the prior using the control.fixed option in the INLA call (see?control.fixed for details). 

Best wishes,

Dan

messages.author: ff1a5632abbf2fe9
messages.subject: Re: Re: [r-inla] Do I need add a intercept to the basic BYM model?
parts:
Thanks
 
Good examples. Anway, I conclude that in INLA All random effect terms are parameterized to include a sum-to-zero constraint to make the model identifiable, which is exactly the same as the WinBUGS.GeoBUGS.
Is this statement correct? 
 
Xing
ZhaoXing
 
From: Daniel Simpson
Date: 2013-07-18 14:30
To: ZhaoXing
Subject: Re: Re: [r-inla] Do I need add a intercept to the basic BYM model?
Sorry. I think I was vague. 
A feature of any funtion in R that takes a formula in the standard way (inla, lm, glm etc) is that it automatically fits an intercept. 

If you *do not* want to fit an intercept, you have to specifically tell R. 

A BYM model with an intercept is
Y~f(region.struct,model="bym",graph.file="germany.graph")
Or
Y~1+f(region.struct,model="bym",graph.file="germany.graph")
(These are equivalent)

A BYM model without an intercept (and, as win bugs says, this is not a good model to fit) is Y~ -1 + f(region.struct,model="bym",graph.file="germany.graph")

The "-1" term says "don't fit an intercept". 

Dan

messages.author: afb003e064114795
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Do I need add a intercept to the basic BYM model?
parts:
On 18 Jul 2013, at 23:32, ZhaoXing <zhaox...@gmail.com> wrote:

Thanks
 
Good examples. Anway, I conclude that in INLA All random effect terms are parameterized to include a sum-to-zero constraint to make the model identifiable, which is exactly the same as the WinBUGS.GeoBUGS.
Is this statement correct?

No, that statement is far to broad, and also does not follow from what Daniel wrote, which was mostly about how R interprets and sets "intercept" terms in formulas.
Only models that are invariant to constants have sum-to-zero constraints enabled by default.  This includes the "besag" model, which the "bym" model builds upon, but many other models are identifiable without a constraint, and therefore by default don't have any constraint  Please see the more detailed documentation for each specific model here:

http://www.r-inla.org/models/latent-models

Finn L

Xing
ZhaoXing
